MANILA, Philippines - The Palace has defended the inclusion of former President Ferdinand Marcos in the Hall of Heroes of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) where portraits of 39 Medal Valor awardees are displayed.

Deputy presidential spokesperson Abigail Valte on Tuesday told reporters that the recognition accorded to the late strongman "does not and cannot include subsequent actions by the recipient."

“These awards continue to be on the official roster of awards of the AFP. Until otherwise revoked, the awardees continue to receive appropriate recognition. It should be noted that the Armed Forces recognizes awardees for the specific deeds that put them on the roster,” Valte said.

She added that while the confernment of the AFP awards is imbued with public interest, "we should note that these awards are generally viewed as non-prtisan and non-political."

Marcos got his Medal of Valor on October 16, 1958 when he was congressman representing the first district of Ilocos Norte under the administration of President Carlos Garcia.

When he was a technical assistant to President Manuel Roxas, Marcos also received the Gold Cross Medal in 1947 and the Distinguished Conduct Star in 1948.

During the term of Elpidio Quirino, Marcos received the Philippine Legion of Honor in 1950.

Under President Diosdado Macapagal, Marcos received the First Bronze Anahaw Leaf to the Distinguished Conduct Star and the First, Second, and Third Bronze Anahaw Leaves to the Gold Cross Medal in 1963.

When he was president, Marcos another Philippine military award - the Second Bronze Anahaw Leaf to the Distinguished Conduct Star.

President Benigno Aquino III earlier tasked Vice President Jejomar Binay to study proposals to allow the burial of Marcos at the Libingan ng mga Bayani.
